question_text: A company wants to add GenAI capabilities to an existing ERP system that uses SOAP/REST APIs and cannot be modified. Which integration pattern minimises coupling?

options.text: Directly couple the FM to the ERP database with read/write permissions
Build an event-driven integration layer: Lambda adapters translate between ERP SOAP calls and the Bedrock API, with EventBridge for loose coupling
Replace the ERP system with a modern platform before adding GenAI
Use Amazon Kendra to index ERP data and treat it as a search problem

explanation: Skill 2.3.1 describes API-based integrations with legacy systems and event-driven architectures for loose coupling. Lambda adapter functions translate between the ERP's protocol and Bedrock's API; EventBridge decouples producers from consumers so the ERP and GenAI layer evolve independently. Direct FM-to-DB coupling is a security and maintenance anti-pattern. Replacing the ERP is a multi-year project — not a GenAI integration approach. Kendra is being retired to new customers and is search-specific.
source_topic: Enterprise integration, event-driven, Lambda, EventBridge

question_text: An enterprise wants employees to invoke Bedrock FMs using their existing corporate identity (Active Directory) without maintaining separate AWS IAM users. Which approach is correct?

options.text: Create individual IAM users for each employee and distribute long-term access keys
Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) to federate with the corporate IdP; employees assume an IAM role via SAML/OIDC to call Bedrock
Share a single IAM role credential across all employees
Embed AWS access keys in the application's front-end JavaScript code

explanation: Skill 2.3.3 describes identity federation between FM services and enterprise systems. IAM Identity Center (SSO) integrates with Active Directory via SAML or OIDC, allowing employees to assume time-limited IAM roles — no long-term keys needed. Individual IAM users with long-term keys are hard to manage at scale and violate least-privilege principles. Shared credentials eliminate per-user auditability. Embedding keys in front-end code is a critical security vulnerability.
source_topic: IAM Identity Center, identity federation, Bedrock access

question_text: A team wants a CI/CD pipeline for their GenAI application that automatically runs prompt regression tests, vulnerability scans, and supports rollback if quality checks fail. Which services should they use? (Choose TWO)

options.text: AWS CodePipeline for pipeline orchestration
AWS CodeBuild for build, test execution, and security scans
Amazon Kendra for indexing deployment artefacts
Amazon Polly for converting deployment logs to audio
Amazon QuickSight for pipeline dashboards

explanation: Skill 2.3.5 explicitly cites AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild for CI/CD pipelines with automated testing frameworks, security scans, and rollback support for GenAI components. CodePipeline orchestrates the stages (source → build → test → deploy); CodeBuild runs the actual build and test commands including prompt regression tests and security scans. Kendra indexes documents — not deployment artefacts. Polly is text-to-speech. QuickSight is BI visualisation, not CI/CD.
source_topic: AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, CI/CD for GenAI

question_text: A financial institution stores sensitive trading data on-premises due to regulatory requirements, but wants to augment GenAI responses with this data without ever sending it to the AWS cloud. Which approach satisfies both constraints?

options.text: Copy the data to Amazon S3 and use Bedrock Knowledge Bases normally
Use AWS Outposts to run Bedrock-compatible infrastructure on-premises, processing data locally
Anonymise all data before uploading to S3
Use a public third-party LLM API that supports on-premises data

explanation: Skill 2.3.4 cites AWS Outposts for on-premises data integration in cross-environment AI solutions. Outposts extends AWS infrastructure into the on-premises environment, allowing data to be processed locally without leaving the premises. Copying to S3 violates the 'no cloud transfer' constraint. Anonymisation may not satisfy strict regulatory requirements for certain data types. Third-party LLM APIs typically require cloud transfer.
source_topic: AWS Outposts, on-premises integration, data sovereignty

question_text: An organisation wants a centralised abstraction layer that provides observability, rate limiting, authentication, and model routing for all internal GenAI consumers. What pattern implements this?

options.text: Give every team direct Bedrock access with separate IAM policies
Deploy a GenAI gateway — API Gateway + Lambda — that centralises auth, rate limiting, logging, and model routing for all consumers
Use S3 presigned URLs to allow teams to call Bedrock
Publish a shared IAM role ARN for all teams to assume

explanation: Skill 2.3.5 describes centralised abstraction layers and observability/control mechanisms as part of secure GenAI gateway architectures. An API Gateway + Lambda gateway centralises: authentication (API keys/Cognito), usage plans and rate limiting, request/response logging, model routing, and cost attribution. Direct team access scatters governance. S3 presigned URLs are for object access — unrelated to Bedrock. A shared IAM role eliminates per-team auditability.
source_topic: GenAI gateway, API Gateway, centralised observability

question_text: An e-commerce platform wants to add a GenAI product recommendation feature to an existing microservices architecture without disrupting other services. Which integration pattern is most appropriate?

options.text: Embed the FM directly into the product catalogue microservice
Create a new GenAI recommendation microservice exposed via API Gateway; existing services call it over its REST API
Add the FM as a database trigger on the product catalogue table
Rewrite all microservices in a single monolith to include the FM

explanation: Skill 2.3.2 describes API Gateway microservice integrations for adding GenAI capabilities to existing applications. A new, isolated GenAI recommendation service with a well-defined API maintains separation of concerns, can be deployed and scaled independently, and minimises blast radius. Embedding the FM inside an existing microservice couples them together and complicates both services. Database triggers are not a GenAI integration mechanism. Monolith migration is counter to microservices principles.
source_topic: Microservice integration, API Gateway, GenAI

topic: Lambda Durable Functions for long-running workflows
question_text: A company runs a multi-step AI document-review workflow: triage → wait for human expert input (up to 3 days) → generate final report. They want a fault-tolerant, serverless implementation that avoids managing state machines or containers. Which new AWS capability fits best?

options.text: Standard AWS Lambda (15-minute timeout) with DynamoDB polling for state
AWS Lambda Durable Functions — checkpoint-aware Lambda that can sleep for up to a year without incurring compute cost
AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow
Amazon ECS Fargate with a persistent container

explanation: AWS Lambda Durable Functions (launched re:Invent Dec 2025, Skill 2.3.1 — enterprise connectivity and Skill 2.5 — development tools) allows sequential, fault-tolerant workflows written as ordinary Lambda code that can suspend for up to ~366 days with no compute cost while waiting. It auto-checkpoints progress so failures replay from the last checkpoint — exactly right for a 3-day human-wait step. Standard Lambda has a 15-minute cap. Step Functions (C) also works for this pattern but requires writing ASL JSON state definitions — more operational complexity than Durable Functions. ECS Fargate incurs continuous cost even when waiting.
source_topic: AWS Lambda Durable Functions, long-running workflows

topic: AppSync GraphQL for multi-source AI queries
question_text: A GenAI dashboard needs to fetch FM-generated summaries, user chat history, and relevant document citations in a single API call to minimise round-trips. Which integration pattern is most appropriate?

options.text: Amazon API Gateway REST API with three separate endpoints, one per data source
AWS AppSync GraphQL API — resolves multiple data sources (Bedrock, DynamoDB, OpenSearch) in one query
An Amazon SQS queue that batches all three requests
AWS Step Functions calling each source sequentially

explanation: AWS AppSync is a managed GraphQL API that can resolve fields from multiple backends (Lambda calling Bedrock, DynamoDB for chat history, OpenSearch for citations) in a single client query, eliminating multi-round-trip overhead (Skill 2.3.2 — integrating AI capabilities into existing applications). REST APIs require separate requests per data source. SQS is asynchronous message queuing — not a synchronous multi-source query resolver. Step Functions calls services sequentially, not in a unified single response.
source_topic: AWS AppSync, GraphQL, multi-source FM integration

topic: AppConfig for dynamic FM selection without code changes
question_text: A team wants to swap the underlying foundation model powering their Bedrock application without redeploying code. New models are released frequently and the team needs to change the model ID in production within minutes of approval. Which AWS service enables this with no code deployment?

options.text: AWS AppConfig — store the model ID as a configuration value; the application reads it at runtime, so changing the config immediately takes effect without a code deployment
AWS CodePipeline — redeploy the Lambda on every model change
AWS CloudFormation — update the stack with the new model ARN each time
Hardcode the model ID in the Lambda environment variable and restart manually

explanation: AWS AppConfig allows configuration values (such as a Bedrock model ID) to be changed dynamically without any code deployment or Lambda restart. The application polls AppConfig at runtime and picks up the new value within seconds. CodePipeline and CloudFormation require deployment pipelines that take minutes and involve code/infra changes. Hardcoded environment variables require a manual redeploy.
source_topic: AppConfig, dynamic FM selection, feature flags

topic: SageMaker Custom Model Import to Bedrock
question_text: A data science team has fine-tuned a custom model in Amazon SageMaker and wants to serve it through the Amazon Bedrock API to benefit from managed serverless inference. What is the correct path?

options.text: Use Bedrock Custom Model Import to import the SageMaker-trained model into Bedrock, then invoke it via the standard Bedrock Converse or InvokeModel API
Directly call the SageMaker endpoint from the client using the Bedrock SDK
Export model weights to S3 and call them directly via a Lambda function
Re-train the model from scratch using Bedrock's fine-tuning job instead

explanation: Bedrock Custom Model Import lets teams bring custom models trained in SageMaker (or elsewhere) into Bedrock, unlocking serverless inference, IAM-based access, Guardrails, and the standard Bedrock APIs. Calling a SageMaker endpoint via the Bedrock SDK does not work — they are separate APIs. Calling raw weights via Lambda bypasses all Bedrock management features. Re-training from scratch discards the existing work.
source_topic: Bedrock Custom Model Import, SageMaker to Bedrock workflow

question_text: An enterprise wants a central control point for all Amazon Bedrock invocations across 30 internal applications. Requirements include: rate limiting per team, logging all prompts/responses to CloudWatch, enforcing cost allocation tags, and hiding model IDs from application teams. What architecture BEST achieves this?

options.text: Have each application team independently configure their own IAM roles and CloudWatch logging
Build a GenAI Gateway using Amazon API Gateway as a centralised proxy in front of Bedrock with usage plans, logging, and cost tagging
Use AWS Service Control Policies to restrict Bedrock access at the OU level
Deploy a Bedrock Guardrail that applies to all invocations

explanation: A GenAI Gateway using API Gateway as a centralised proxy provides all required capabilities: usage plans for per-team rate limiting, request/response logging to CloudWatch, tagging for cost allocation, and abstraction of backend model IDs from callers. Per-team independent IAM roles don't centralise control. SCPs restrict access broadly but don't provide per-team rate limits or observability. Guardrails enforce content safety, not operational governance.
source_topic: GenAI Gateway with API Gateway for centralised governance

question_text: A team wants to automatically deploy updates to their GenAI application's Lambda functions and Bedrock Guardrails configuration when code is merged to the main branch, with automated rollback if CloudWatch alarms trigger within 5 minutes of deployment. Which AWS services enable this pipeline?

options.text: AWS CodeCommit + AWS CodePipeline + AWS CodeDeploy with CloudWatch alarm rollback
AWS Glue + Amazon EMR + CloudWatch
Amazon SageMaker Pipelines + Amazon EventBridge
AWS Step Functions + AWS Lambda + Amazon SNS

explanation: CodePipeline orchestrates the CI/CD workflow. CodeDeploy deploys Lambda functions with traffic shifting (canary/linear) and natively supports CloudWatch alarm-based automatic rollback. CloudWatch alarms trigger the rollback if error rates spike within the monitoring window. Glue + EMR is for data pipelines. SageMaker Pipelines is for ML training. Step Functions + Lambda can implement custom CI/CD but lacks CodeDeploy's native traffic shifting and alarm rollback.
source_topic: CI/CD for GenAI with CodePipeline + CodeDeploy alarm rollback

question_text: A company has a legacy SAP system that generates new purchase orders as events. They want each new order to automatically trigger a Bedrock-powered analysis and store the result in DynamoDB. Which integration pattern minimises custom code?

options.text: Poll SAP via Lambda every minute and check for new orders
Configure SAP to publish events to Amazon EventBridge, trigger Lambda for Bedrock analysis, store result in DynamoDB
Dump SAP data to S3 daily and run a Glue ETL job
Replicate the SAP database to RDS and query it from Lambda

explanation: EventBridge is the preferred event-driven integration pattern for connecting enterprise/SaaS systems (including SAP) to AWS services. SAP publishes events, EventBridge routes them to a Lambda function that calls Bedrock and writes to DynamoDB — all event-driven with minimal code. Polling every minute wastes compute and adds latency. Daily S3 dumps are near-batch, not real-time. Database replication is complex and doesn't react to individual events.
source_topic: EventBridge for enterprise system event-driven integration

question_text: A front-end developer needs to quickly add a Bedrock-powered chat interface to a React web application without building backend infrastructure from scratch. Which AWS service provides pre-built UI components and backend integration for GenAI chat experiences?

options.text: AWS AppSync
Amazon API Gateway + Lambda (custom build)
AWS Amplify with AI/GenAI UI components
Amazon Lex

explanation: AWS Amplify provides pre-built UI components for AI/chat experiences and integrates directly with Amazon Bedrock — enabling developers to add GenAI chat interfaces to React, Vue, or Angular apps with minimal backend work. AppSync is a managed GraphQL API service. API Gateway + Lambda requires building the entire backend manually. Amazon Lex is a conversational interface service, not a front-end UI component library.
source_topic: AWS Amplify AI components for rapid GenAI UI development

question_text: An existing e-commerce platform built on microservices wants to add AI-powered product descriptions without modifying existing services. How should the GenAI capability be added with the LEAST disruption to existing architecture?

options.text: Refactor all product services to embed Bedrock calls directly
Add a new GenAI microservice exposed via API Gateway that existing services call when they need AI-enhanced descriptions
Replace the product catalogue service with a Bedrock-native implementation
Deploy the new AI feature directly on the existing product service's EC2 instances

explanation: Adding GenAI as a new microservice exposed via API Gateway follows the strangler fig pattern — adding capability without modifying existing services. Existing services call the new endpoint when AI-enhanced content is needed, and the new service handles all Bedrock interactions. Refactoring existing services is disruptive. Replacing services entirely is risky. Co-deploying on existing EC2 instances creates coupling and limits scalability.
source_topic: GenAI as a new microservice for additive integration

question_text: A Bedrock-based application in eu-west-1 needs to call a model only available in us-east-1 while keeping all application infrastructure in Europe. The invocation must stay on the AWS private network. What is the CORRECT setup?

options.text: Route the call via the public internet using a VPN
Configure the Lambda in eu-west-1 to call the Bedrock endpoint in us-east-1 using AWS SDK cross-region call over the AWS backbone network
Deploy an EC2 proxy in us-east-1 to relay Bedrock calls from eu-west-1
Use CloudFront to cache model responses globally

explanation: AWS SDK calls between regions travel over the AWS private backbone network, not the public internet. The Lambda function in eu-west-1 simply specifies the us-east-1 Bedrock endpoint in the SDK client configuration with appropriate IAM permissions. No proxy is needed. VPN adds unnecessary complexity. A relay EC2 adds cost and management overhead. CloudFront caches static content, not dynamic LLM inference.
source_topic: Cross-region Bedrock call via AWS SDK

question_text: An enterprise with thousands of employees in Active Directory wants to allow employees to access an internal Amazon Q Business application using their existing corporate credentials. Which AWS service enables federated identity for this scenario?

options.text: Amazon Cognito User Pools with a custom user database
IAM Identity Center (SSO) with SAML or OIDC integration to Active Directory
Individual IAM users for each employee
Amazon Lex with authentication challenge flows

explanation: IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO) is the recommended solution for enterprise identity federation — it integrates with Active Directory (or any SAML/OIDC identity provider) and provides single-sign-on access to AWS applications like Amazon Q Business. Creating individual IAM users for thousands of employees is operationally impossible. Cognito is for customer-facing apps, not internal corporate users. Lex is a chatbot service, not an identity provider.
source_topic: IAM Identity Center for corporate Active Directory federation

question_text: A CISO wants to ensure that across ALL AWS accounts in the organisation, only approved Amazon Bedrock models (specified by model ID) can be invoked — even if an account's IAM policies are misconfigured. Which control enforces this ORG-WIDE restriction that CANNOT be overridden by individual account IAM?

options.text: IAM permission boundaries on every IAM role
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applied to all invocations
AWS Service Control Policy (SCP) with a bedrock:ModelId condition key
AWS Config rules that alert on unapproved model invocations

explanation: AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) are applied at the AWS Organizations level and create maximum permission boundaries that CANNOT be overridden by IAM policies in member accounts. An SCP with a `aws:RequestedRegion` or `bedrock:ModelId` condition can deny invocations of unapproved models across all accounts. IAM permission boundaries apply per-role and can be misconfigured at account level. Guardrails enforce content safety, not model ID restrictions. AWS Config detects violations but doesn't prevent them.
source_topic: SCP with bedrock:ModelId for org-wide model governance

question_text: A healthcare company's Lambda function must call Amazon Bedrock without any traffic leaving the AWS network or traversing the public internet. What is the CORRECT networking configuration?

options.text: Configure the Lambda function in a VPC with a NAT Gateway for Bedrock access
Configure a VPC Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) for Amazon Bedrock in the VPC where Lambda runs
Use an ALB in front of Bedrock to route traffic privately
Deploy Lambda outside a VPC — Bedrock calls are private by default

explanation: A VPC Interface Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for Amazon Bedrock keeps all traffic between the VPC and Bedrock on the AWS private network — no internet gateway, NAT gateway, or public IP required. This is the required configuration for strict 'no public internet' compliance. A NAT Gateway routes to the public internet. An ALB is a load balancer, not a private network endpoint. Lambda outside a VPC uses the public endpoint by default.
source_topic: VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) for private Bedrock access

question_text: A government agency requires that all AI inference for a sensitive application must be physically performed on-premises due to strict data sovereignty requirements. Which AWS solution supports running Bedrock-compatible services on-premises?

options.text: AWS Local Zones
AWS Wavelength
AWS Outposts
AWS Direct Connect

explanation: AWS Outposts brings AWS infrastructure and services physically on-premises, enabling applications to run in the customer's data center under their physical control — meeting strict data sovereignty requirements. Local Zones are AWS-managed edge facilities, not customer premises. Wavelength is for 5G/edge latency, not data residency on-prem. Direct Connect is a private network link from on-prem to AWS cloud, not on-prem compute.
source_topic: AWS Outposts for on-premises data sovereignty

question_text: A company needs to transfer 50 TB of on-premises documents to Amazon S3 for use in a Bedrock Knowledge Base. The transfer must happen reliably over a Direct Connect link. Which AWS service is BEST suited for this large-scale, reliable file transfer?

options.text: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
AWS DataSync
Amazon AppFlow
AWS Snowball

explanation: AWS DataSync is purpose-built for large-scale, reliable data transfers between on-premises storage and AWS (S3, EFS, FSx) over Direct Connect or internet connections. It handles scheduling, monitoring, verification, and delta transfers. Kinesis Firehose is for streaming data pipelines. AppFlow is for SaaS application data transfers. Snowball is for offline, physical device transfers (petabyte scale or where network is unavailable).
source_topic: AWS DataSync for on-premises to S3 large file transfer

topic: Q Business vs Bedrock Knowledge Bases
question_text: A company wants to deploy an enterprise search and Q&A assistant that connects to SharePoint, Confluence, S3, and Salesforce — with built-in access control so users only see documents they have permission to access. They want minimal custom development. Which AWS service BEST meets this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with custom Lambda connectors
Amazon Q Business with built-in data connectors and ACL-aware retrieval
Amazon OpenSearch Service with custom ingestion pipelines
Amazon Kendra with custom connectors

explanation: Amazon Q Business provides a fully managed enterprise GenAI assistant with built-in connectors for SharePoint, Confluence, S3, Salesforce, and many others. Critically, it respects source document access control lists (ACLs) so users only see results they are permitted to access — without custom code. Bedrock Knowledge Bases requires custom Lambda connectors for most SaaS sources. OpenSearch requires building all ingestion and ACL logic. Kendra is a search service being closed to new customers (July 2026).
source_topic: Amazon Q Business for ACL-aware enterprise search
